## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Restore the deleted defaults file before merge because `load_defaults()` still requires it. This review also found an incorrect port boundary, silent configuration failures, an uncovered normalization branch, and an inaccurate docstring. All changed files and existing tests were read; no tests were run.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization with tests. It also deletes the defaults file and adds reviewer documentation and a fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the defaults file required by startup — Calling `load_defaults()` after this deletion raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning `{"timeout": 30}`. The unchanged reader at `app/startup.py:6` still opens this exact file. — Users calling `load_defaults()` can no longer load the application defaults.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Include port 65535 in the valid range — For `is_valid_port(65535)`, your validator returns `False` even though its documented range includes 65535. The strict upper comparison excludes that valid boundary. — Callers incorrectly reject configurations using TCP port 65535.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Expose configuration loading failures to callers — For a missing file or malformed JSON, your handler discards `FileNotFoundError` or the decoding exception and returns `{}`. Neither a log nor a caller signal distinguishes failure from successfully loading an empty object, and no adjacent explanation documents that behavior as intentional. — Users cannot distinguish a broken configuration from an empty configuration or identify what needs correcting.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Test trailing-dot removal — For `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`, no test exercises the trailing-dot branch; returning `"example.com."` would go undetected. The sole host test uses `"Example.COM"` and covers only lowercasing. — Regression protection does not cover the newly added trailing-dot normalization behavior.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the empty-host docstring with the return value — For `normalize_host("")`, your docstring says “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`. — Callers relying on the documentation receive a different empty-value sentinel than promised.
